items.name: Aaron Levie
items.text: It’s almost incomprehensible how wide the distance is between someone who’s working at the frontier with AI and basically everyone else right now. The crazy thing is these lines are not converging, but only growing farther apart. If the curve of AI progress had leveled off, it would certainly have given most people and companies time to catch up or implement their workflows in a standardized way. The technology would have neutralized competitive advantage because everyone would be using it the same way. But what’s happened is the opposite. The curve of AI progress is basically going vertical right now, which means if you had codified your processes 3-6 months ago you’re likely already behind again. Now imagine most companies that kicked into gear a year ago and thought that they were done. Even further behind now. I’ve never seen a technology in my life and career that improves at this rate, which consequently means you need to upgrade your expectations at a similar rate. Our brains weren’t wired for this, and our organizational change management processes certainly weren’t either. With any form of recursive self improvement, things just get wilder. It’s a time when you will need to be constantly reevaluating the things that didn’t work just a couple months ago to see if they now can be solved. AI native companies certainly have a strong advantage due to this right now, so now it comes down to can the bigger companies keep up. Wild times.

items.text: big boy warm tension, cold chills heart hanging off a cliff, ready to free fall floating in space with no love, just me and some stranger souls wearing smiles and greet “How are you?” “I’m good, you?” life carries on, unhinged a tear slips, no one noticed vision blurs, drowned in thoughts what a strange grown-up world i asked my inner child, why do you live? he has never thought about it he slid on the cold iced river, amused he sang, he played, he drew he flew into the unknown, fearless, curious he closed his eyes and saw wonders like water, with no shape like paper, clear of rules “Why cry, big boy?” “You are still me, and I’m still you.”
